heading: Workplace Therapy
body:
Mental health within the workplace is an often overlooked element of wellbeing. But this is an issue that has an impact on individuals and organisations. In 2024/25 over 900,000 workers experienced work-related stress, anxiety or depression – leading to the loss of 22.1 million working days (HSE, 2025).
 
I have worked with companies such as LADBible and Genuit Group to provide therapy and support for their employees. Through this work, I've seen fewer mental-health-related absences, smoother returns to work and better staff retention.  

Employee feedback has highlighted positive impacts such as reduced stress and anxiety around work, improved relationships with colleagues and an appreciation for the human-focused culture their organisation has adopted. 

It is also vital that I work closely with the organisation, as this allows managers and leaders to make referrals if they identify a member of the team who would benefit from therapy. It also allows me to liaise with HR to make recommendations regarding absent staff and supporting their return to work. My service remains confidential and I do not disclose details, but this collaboration means support is holistic and integrated into workplace culture. Another element of my work is mental health and wellbeing advocacy, so I often inform and advise organisations on how they can better support their employees and how best to implement the appropriate steps.

Organisations I've worked with have told me they've seen increased productivity and outcomes from employees receiving therapy, less time lost to absences and more confidence in their ability to effectively support individuals in and out of work.
